title: Prepositional 2: After 'на'
description: After 'на' (on/at), the noun shifts to the prepositional case. Same forms as after 'в.' Today also introduces feminine -я → -е.
descriptionRussian: После 'на' существительное переходит в предложный падеж. Те же формы, что и после 'в.' Сегодня вводится женский -я → -е.
intro: На is the second location preposition, and it takes the same endings as в, so today asks almost nothing new of the noun. Choosing between the two is a genuinely hard problem, and doing that at the same time as producing a case ending is what makes learners feel Russian is impossible. Get the ending automatic first. Lesson 3 gives you the choice.
rules: На is the second main location preposition. Like в, it triggers the prepositional case. The case forms are identical to those used after в: + -е for masc consonant, -а → -е for fem -а.
Feminine nouns ending in -я swap -я for -е, just like fem -а: кухня → на кухне, неделя → на неделе. Soft -я becomes soft -е.
The choice between в and на depends on the noun's category (drilled in Lesson 3). Today, accept the preposition the prompt gives you and apply the case rule.
examples: Маша на работе. (Masha is at work.) работа → на работе.
Книга на столе. (The book is on the table.) стол → на столе.
Антон на концерте. (Anton is at the concert.) концерт → на концерте.
Я на улице. (I am on the street.) улица → на улице.
Они на кухне. (They are in the kitchen.) кухня → на кухне.

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 1: what ending did the noun take after 'в'?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 1: после 'в' (location), masculine consonant nouns take prepositional + -е. Магазин → в магазине. Today's lesson uses 'на' in the same way for different categories of place.

items.promptEnglish: The book is on the table.
items.hint: На is also a location preposition. What ending does the masculine consonant take?
items.explanation: На triggers prepositional just like в does. The case forms are identical: masc consonant takes -е. Стол → на столе.

items.hint: Работа is feminine -а. Apply the same rule as Lesson 1.
items.explanation: На followed by feminine -а: same swap -а → -е we saw with 'в школе.' Работа → на работе. Russians say 'на работе' (at work) but 'в офисе' (in the office). The choice between 'на' and 'в' depends on the noun, not the case rule. Lesson 3 drills this.

items.hint: Кухня ends in -я. The soft -я swaps to which vowel?
items.explanation: Кухня ends in -я. Feminine -я follows the same pattern as feminine -а: it swaps to -е. Кухня → на кухне. Notice: -я (soft) becomes -е (soft). The soft ending stays soft.

items.hint: Концерт is masculine consonant. Apply the rule.
items.explanation: Концерт → на концерте. The masculine pattern is consistent across both 'в' and 'на.' The trigger preposition does not change the case form.

Улица → на улице. Russian uses 'на' for location 'on the street' rather than 'в' (which would be 'inside the street'). The form is determined by gender; the choice of в vs на is determined by the noun's category.

blanks: Антон на _____. (Anton is at the stadium.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Стадион is masculine consonant. Prepositional after 'на': add -е → стадионе.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The book is lying on the chair.
errorCorrection.explanation: На triggers the prepositional case for location just as в does, and masculine consonant nouns add -е: на стуле. Стул here is the bare nominative. The accusative стул follows на only for motion onto a surface ('положи книгу на стул').

Feminine nouns ending in -я take -е in the prepositional, exactly like feminine -а nouns: деревня → в деревне. The soft -я becomes a soft -е, not -и. Both в and на trigger the same prepositional case for location.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The children are playing at the stadium.
errorCorrection.explanation: Стадион is a на-word for location ('at the stadium'), and location after на takes the prepositional: на стадионе. Стадион unchanged is the bare nominative, which cannot express location.

minimalPairs.explanation: After 'на' (location), the noun shifts to the prepositional case: работе. The nominative работа would be a subject: 'Работа интересная' (The work is interesting).
After 'на' (location), the noun shifts to the prepositional case: кухне. The fem -я → -е pattern parallels the fem -а → -е pattern from Lesson 1.

reviewVocab.definition: on / at (preposition + prepositional, used for surfaces, events, and some specific places)
work / job (Russian says 'на работе' for 'at work,' not 'в работе')
lesson / class (Russian says 'на уроке' for 'at the lesson')
